NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  In accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), City Council Resolution Nos. 2487, 2490, 2491, 2493,
  2498, 2499, 2503, 2505, 2507, 2512, 2519, 2521, 2530 and proposed Resolution No. 2534, due to the
  continuing state of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat
  of the COVID-19 virus, this meeting is being broadcast via teleconference. Members of the public may
  participate in-person in the Council Chambers, or virtually in the meeting in the following ways:

  - Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling 1-669-900-6833 from any phone, Meeting
  ID: 869 7686 4391, Meeting Password: 066081. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using
  the call in option from a phone line.)

  - Public correspondence may be emailed to the City Clerk at laurenp@rollinghillsestates.gov. Emails
  received before 3:00 p.m. prior to the start of the meeting will be forwarded to the City Council for their
  consideration and included as part of the record.

  - Members of the public may also comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes &
  Videos” page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there
  will be an “eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to
  the City’s SpeakUp page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda.
  These comments can be seen by the public, will be considered by the Council and become part of the
  record.

  - Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
  Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store),
  by entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 869 7686 4391, Meeting Password: 066081. Members
  of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the following
  process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at the
  lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
  agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City's website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  NOVEMBER 8, 2022

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order
by MAYOR ZERUNYAN at 7:08 p.m. in the Council Chambers of City Hall and remotely via
teleconference, in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 (AB 361), due to the continuing state
of emergency, including masking and social distancing directives as a result of the threat of
the COVID-19 virus.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by local students from Rolling Robots.

Mayor Zerunyan presented certificates of recognition to the Rolling Robots teams for winning
the 2022 VEX Robotics World Championship Middle School Division.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead
  Public Works Director David Wahba
  Community Development Director Jeannie Naughton
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Management Analyst Jessica Slawson
  Associate Planner Dean Flores

4.  CEREMONIAL

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING NOVEMBER 26, 2022 AS "SMALL BUSINESS
  SATURDAY"

MAYOR ZERUNYAN presented the Proclamation to Eileen Hupp, President of the Palos
Verdes Peninsula Chamber of Commerce, and declared November 26, 2022 as “Small
Business Saturday.”

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
NOVEMBER 8, 2022
 7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

A.  APPEAL OF PLANNING COMMISSION DECISION FOR PLANNING APPLICATION
  NO. 220241
  APPLICANT: DAVE & HELEN SHAW
  LOCATION: 19 BUCKSKIN LANE

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1. Open the Public Hearing; 2. Take Public
  Testimony; 3. Discuss the issues; 4. Close the Public Hearing; and 5. Approve
  Resolution No. 2532 upholding the Planning Commission’s decision to deny both
  Variance Application No. V-220243 and Neighborhood Compatibility Application No.
  NC-220242, requiring the applicant to demolish or relocate the unpermitted
  accessory structures to comply with code, and determining the disapproval of the
  applications to be exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act under CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15270(a).

**MAYOR ZERUNYAN recused himself and left the Chambers at 7:25 pm.

Associate Planner Flores provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Director Wahba explained that the horse washing slab was not considered by the Planning
Commission, but that staff could look into whether or not proper drainage was added, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Public Works Director Wahba clarified that the applicant owns both properties, 19 Buckskin
Lane and 2715 Palos Verdes Drive North, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING.

Appellant David Shaw provided a presentation outlining the work that was done at the property
on 19 Buckskin Lane, and the reasons for his appeal to the Planning Commission’s decision.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA discussed how setbacks are described in the Municipal Code,
which requires a seven foot distance between the building and the property line.

Appellant Shaw explained that he put the buildings in the same place the original buildings
existed, and is requesting a variance, in response to MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF.

City Attorney noted for the record that code enforcement is an anonymous process.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. Public testimony was received by Tim Zigrang, who spoke in favor of allowing
the structures to remain in place.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ summarized the difficulty in making this decision, and the deep
thought and consideration the Council puts into any decision.

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF asked Director Wahba about the Planning Commission’s discussion
regarding this application.

COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN noted that no one on the Planning Commission or City
Council have been able to make the findings to allow this exception/variance.

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA echoed the sentiments of the Council that this is a difficult
decision to make.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
NOVEMBER 8, 2022
   APPROVE RESOLUTION NO. 2532 UPHOLDING THE PLANNING
  COMMISSION’S DECISION TO DENY BOTH VARIANCE APPLICATION NO.
  V-220243 AND NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY APPLICATION NO. NC-
  220242, REQUIRING THE APPLICANT TO DEMOLISH OR RELOCATE THE
  UNPERMITTED ACCESSORY STRUCTURES TO COMPLY WITH CODE,
  AND DETERMINING THE DISAPPROVAL OF THE APPLICATIONS TO BE
  EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT
  UNDER CEQA GUIDELINES SECTION.

  AYES:  Schmitz, Stegura and Zuckerman
  NOES:  Huff
  ABSTAIN:  Zerunyan

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2532 by title.

**MAYOR ZERUNYAN returned to the Chambers at 8:38 pm.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  COMMISSION AND COMMITTEE LOCAL APPOINTMENT  LIST  AND
  APPOINTMENT PROCESS FOR EXPIRING TERMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council review the Commission/Committee
  appointment process for expiring terms, and receive and file this report.

City Clerk Pettit provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

City Clerk Pettit explained the recruitment process following the Council’s approval, in response
to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

B.  PA-220218: LOCAL EARLY ACTION PLANNING (LEAP) GRANT PROGRAM - SB
  743 IMPLEMENTATION ADOPTING A NEW CEQA VEHICLE MILES TRAVELED
  (VMT) POLICY

  Recommendation: Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No.
  2533, adopting a policy to comply with SB 743 and CEQA requirements to establish
  vehicle miles traveled (VMT) as the metric used to determine the CEQA-related
  transportation impacts of new development and transportation projects, and
  determining that the adoption of the VMT policy is categorically exempt from CEQA.

Public Works Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Fehr & Peers Consultant John Muggridge provided a presentation on Senate Bill 743, CEQA
Analysis and Non-CEQA Analysis.

Consultant Muggridge explained that the VMT plan is consistent with a number of local
jurisdictions that also have VMT requirements, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER
ZUCKERMAN.

Discussion ensued regarding the range of mitigation options for Rolling Hills Estates, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
NOVEMBER 8, 2022
 COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN expressed concern about the 10,000 mile VMT average
being used, as well as the City’s ability to reduce VMT while meeting the State’s housing
requirements.

Discussion ensued regarding VMT calculations including electric vehicles.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2533, ADOPTING A POLICY TO COMPLY WITH
  SB 743 AND CEQA REQUIREMENTS TO ESTABLISH VEHICLE MILES
  TRAVELED (VMT) AS THE METRIC USED TO DETERMINE THE CEQA-
  RELATED TRANSPORTATION IMPACTS OF NEW DEVELOPMENT AND
  TRANSPORTATION PROJECTS, AND DETERMINING THAT THE
  ADOPTION OF THE VMT POLICY IS CATEGORICALLY EXEMPT FROM
  CEQA.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan and Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  None

City Clerk Pettit read Resolution No. 2533 by title.

C.  PENINSULA UTILITY WHITE PAPER ON DISASTER RESPONSE

  Recommendation: That the Council receive and file this report.

Management Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chambers, via email, via eComment, and
during the live Zoom Webinar as noticed on the Agenda and on the City’s website and social
media platforms. No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS:

  RECEIVE AND FILE.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN so ordered.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  UPDATE ON LOS ANGELES COUNTY SAFER AT HOME ORDER (VERBAL
  REPORT)

City Manager Grammer reported that there have been no changes to the current Los Angeles
County Health Officer Order.

City Manager Grammer welcomed back Jeannie Naughton as the new Community
Development Director and noted that David Wahba would now serve as the Public Works
Director.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

None.

11.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

MAYOR PRO TEM HUFF attended the recent Neighborhood Watch Council meeting.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 8, 2022
 COUNCIL MEMBER ZUCKERMAN attended the recent Clean Power Alliance Board of
Directors meeting, where the annual audit was discussed.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

MAYOR ZERUNYAN congratulated Administrative Services Director Mike Whitehead for
receiving an award for achievement in information technology practices from Municipal
Information Systems Association of California (MIASC).

MAYOR ZERUNYAN also announced that the City of Rolling Hills Estates has received a
Certificate of Achievement for Excellence in Financial Reporting from the Government Finance
Officers Association (GFOA) for our FY 2020-21 Annual Comprehensive Financial Report.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN also noted there will be a dedication ceremony this Saturday, November
12 for public art at City Hall, as well as the Promenade’s Tree Lighting Ceremony on Saturday
November 17.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Government Code Section 54957
  Title: City Manager 6:30pm (Quarterly Evaluation)

  NO REPORTABLE ACTION

14.  ADJOURNMENT

At 9:28 p.m. MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the City Council meeting in memory of Herbert
Tan and Donald Gould. The meeting was adjourned to Tuesday, November 22, 2022, at
7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a Regular Meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Lauren Pettit  Frank V. Zerunyan
City Clerk  Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
NOVEMBER 8, 2022
